name: StrongDM
scope_notes: SaaS control plane (US/UK/EU); Log Stream and 13-month log viewing require the Enterprise plan, other plans see 30 days in the Admin UI.

controls.name: Delete token
controls.what: Deleting an admin token stops it authenticating immediately.
controls.setting: Principals > Tokens; sdm admin tokens delete

controls.name: Rotate
controls.what: Generates a new secret with the same permissions; existing authentications expire after 24 hours.

controls.name: Token permissions
controls.what: Each admin token or API key gets only the admin permissions chosen at creation.
controls.setting: Create Admin Token / Create API Key page; --permissions

controls.name: Token expiry
controls.what: Set an expiry at creation; 'never' is an allowed choice.

controls.name: Delete API key
controls.what: Deleted API keys are invalidated instantly.
controls.setting: Principals > Tokens; sdm admin tokens delete

controls.name: Delete tokens on user suspension
controls.what: When suspending a user, the Admin UI lists their tokens and keys and asks whether to delete them.

controls.name: Role membership
controls.what: Service accounts only reach resources granted through their roles.

controls.name: Suspend user
controls.what: Suspending an account revokes its access to infrastructure.

controls.name: Permission level: Manage service accounts, admin tokens, and API keys
controls.what: Only the Administrator permission level can create or manage admin tokens, API keys, and service accounts; other levels cannot.

controls.name: Permission level: Manage relays and gateways
controls.what: Only Administrators can create gateways/relays and so obtain node tokens.

controls.name: Permission level: Update account settings
controls.what: Only Administrators can change org settings, where SCIM is activated and its token generated.

controls.name: SCIM Provider: None - provisioning disabled
controls.what: Turns off SCIM provisioning for the org.
controls.setting: Settings > User Management > Provisioning > SCIM Provider

controls.name: Policies (Location::IP context)
controls.what: Cedar policy statements can permit or forbid a principal's resource actions based on the source IP or location.

controls.name: sdm admin users suspend --cascade
controls.what: Suspending a user with --cascade also suspends that user's linked API keys.

controls.name: sdm admin nodes delete
controls.what: Deletes a gateway or relay node.

no_control.what: API keys cannot be rotated in place.
Suspending the creating user does not disable admin tokens.
Suspending the creating user does not disable API keys.

controls_unknown: Any IP allowlist for admin tokens, API keys, service accounts, or SCIM tokens (docs silent).
Any org-wide switch to block creation of admin tokens or API keys, or a maximum expiry policy.
Whether SSO-required or MFA settings apply to service account token logins.
SCIM token rotation, revocation, and lifetime.
Service account token lifetime and rekey procedure.
Whether read-only SDK/API calls (e.g. listing accounts or resources) are recorded as Activities.
Whether API key creation logs as 'Admin token created' or a separate event.

authentication.summary: Single secret string used with the sdm CLI via SDM_ADMIN_TOKEN or sdm login --admin-token. It can only run the sdm admin commands granted to it, and use skips the interactive login.

federation.details: Static secret; no documented workload identity federation.

ip_restriction.boundary: Docs do not describe any IP allowlist for admin tokens.

lifetime.summary: 1 week, 1 month, 1 year, or never (CLI duration default 0)

renewal.summary: Rotate regenerates the secret with same name and permissions; old authentications expire after 24 hours.

administration.summary: Admins create, list, rotate and delete in Principals > Tokens or sdm admin tokens. Tokens survive suspension of the creating user unless deleted.
administration.conditions: Administrator permission level needed to create via CLI.

sso.details: Docs say a CLI session using an admin token does not need a CLI or GUI login, so the SSO login flow is not involved.

offboard.details: Admin tokens keep working after the creating user is suspended unless the admin chooses to delete them in the suspension prompt.

inventory.details: Admin UI Principals > Tokens and `sdm admin tokens list` list all tokens in the org; `sdm audit tokens` gives a point-in-time listing.

token_format.notes: Opaque string shown once; prefix not documented.

log_sources.name: Activities (Admin UI Logs > Activities, sdm audit activities, API Activities)
log_sources.notes: 30 days in Admin UI without Enterprise, 13 months with Enterprise.

log_sources.name: Log Stream - Activities
log_sources.notes: Enterprise; streams to customer object storage.

credential_id_fields.notes: Account that performed the activity; whether token ID is separately recorded is not documented.

anomaly_cues: Admin activity from unfamiliar ipAddress or userAgent

containment.steps: Delete the token in Principals > Tokens or with sdm admin tokens delete. Prefer delete over rotate: rotation lets existing authentications live up to 24 hours.
containment.notes: Docs say delete is immediate, but the rotate tooltip says existing authentications expire after 24 hours.

unknown: Whether each admin command run with the token is an Activity

calls.log_notes: Activities cover administrative changes; reads not stated.

calls.call: sdm admin datasources list / sdm admin servers list

unknown: No documented whoami for admin tokens

authentication.summary: Access key (auth-...) plus secret used by the SDKs and Terraform provider to sign each gRPC request, AWS SigV4 style; the secret is not sent.

federation.details: Static key pair; no documented federation.

ip_restriction.boundary: Docs do not describe any IP allowlist for API keys.

renewal.summary: No rotation; clone to create a new pair with the same permissions, then delete the old one.

administration.summary: Admins view, add, clone and delete keys in Principals > Tokens; permissions are fixed at creation. Keys survive suspension of the creating user.

offboard.details: API keys survive suspension of the creating user by default; the UI prompt or `sdm admin users suspend --cascade` can suspend/delete them.

inventory.details: Admin UI Principals > Tokens lists API keys; `sdm admin tokens list` lists all tokens in the org.

usage.ui: Logs > Activities; filter Actor/Account = API key owner (activities such as 'Admin token ...')
usage.cli: sdm audit activities --from <date> --json, then filter on actorAccountID

offboard.ui: Users > Actions > Suspend user > Confirm suspension; answer Yes when prompted to delete the user's API keys

token_format.notes: Access key is a hex string auth-...; older keys used a long Base64 string.

log_sources.name: Activities
log_sources.notes: 30 days in Admin UI without Enterprise, 13 months with Enterprise; Log Stream is Enterprise.

containment.steps: Delete the key in Principals > Tokens; there is no rotate, so create a replacement first if automation needs it.
containment.notes: Signed requests are checked per call, so deletion blocks further requests.

unknown: Exact Activity names for API key create/delete

calls.reveals: Infrastructure inventory and who can reach it

calls.log_notes: Activities record userAgent and ipAddress when an activity is logged.

authentication.summary: A service account is a non-human user that logs in with its token (sdm login --admin-token or the desktop app) and then gets resource access through role membership.

federation.details: No documented OIDC/workload federation for service accounts.

ip_restriction.boundary: Enterprise Policies (Cedar) can permit/forbid resource actions by context.location IP for any principal, including service accounts. No documented IP restriction on the token login itself.

lifetime.summary: Optional expiration set when creating the service account (CLI CSV name,expiration); 'Service account expired' activity is logged

renewal.summary: Activities include 'Service account rekeyed'; rekey procedure not documented on the service account page.

administration.summary: Admins create service accounts in Principals > Users > Add service; access is limited by role membership; accounts can be suspended.

sso.details: Service accounts authenticate with tokens instead of username/password, and session/idle timeouts apply only to human users.

offboard.details: Service accounts are machine principals, not tied to a human user.

inventory.details: `sdm admin services list` lists all service accounts; Principals > Users shows them with a Service Account label.

expiry.cli: sdm admin services add --csv (CSV columns name,expiration); expiry is logged as activity 'Service account expired'

usage.ui: Logs > Activities (and Logs > Queries) filtered by Account = service account
usage.cli: sdm audit activities --json (filter actorAccountID); sdm audit queries --from <date>

log_sources.name: Activities
log_sources.notes: Plus Queries and Replays for resource sessions when StrongDM log retention is enabled.

lifecycle_events.event: Attempted to login by a suspended service account from the Admin UI

anomaly_cues: Service account logins from new IPs
Resource queries outside normal job windows

containment.steps: Suspend the service account in Users, or rekey it.
containment.notes: Effect on open resource sessions not documented.

unknown: Whether suspension ends live client sessions

calls.reveals: Resources the service account can reach
calls.log_notes: Resource connections are logged as queries/replays, not Activities.

authentication.summary: Bearer token generated when an admin activates SCIM provisioning; the IdP uses it against /provisioning/<provider>/v2 endpoints on app.strongdm.com to manage users and roles.

administration.summary: Created at Settings > User Management > Provisioning by activating SCIM.

offboard.details: SCIM token belongs to the org provisioning integration, not a user.

usage.ui: Logs > Activities (only 'SCIM token created' is listed; no per-call SCIM log)

anomaly_cues: User/role changes via SCIM not matching IdP changes

containment.steps: Not documented; deactivating SCIM provisioning in Settings > User Management > Provisioning is the likely path.

unknown: Whether SCIM requests are logged as Activities

authentication.summary: Token generated when creating a gateway or relay node; installed on the host (SDM_RELAY_TOKEN) so the node can join the organization's network.

ip_restriction.boundary: Docs say a node's IP cannot be changed after creation, but do not describe this as a token IP restriction.

lifetime.summary: Node removed after 30 days with no heartbeat

renewal.summary: Replace by creating a new node and putting its token on the host.

administration.summary: Created and deleted under Networking > Gateways/Relays; Activities record Relay created/deleted.

offboard.details: Gateway/relay tokens belong to a node, not a user.

inventory.details: Admin UI Gateways and Relays pages and `sdm admin nodes list` list all nodes.

usage.ui: Logs > Activities (relay/gateway lifecycle events such as 'Relay created')

anomaly_cues: New relays or gateways not created by infrastructure automation

containment.steps: Delete the node in Networking and create a new one with a new token.

unknown: Whether deleting a node disconnects it immediately
What a stolen node token can do beyond registering a node is not documented
